description: Make the initiate page (InitiateSignature.tsx) support batch mode. Refactor the single-document save into a reusable createProcessForDocument helper (no single-flow behavior change), then detect the new `fileRefs` query param to run per-document configuration (approvers + placeholders separately per document) with navigation, per-document validation, and a batch submit that creates one Approvals Process item per document all sharing one BatchId with BatchMode=AllOrNothing. Depends on FEAT-001's fileRefs contract.
steps: In src/webparts/initiateSignature/components/InitiateSignature.tsx, extract the per-document creation logic currently inside handleSaveWorkflow (QR embed + setContentChunked overwrite, generatePDFHash, build ProcessSignature JSON from approvers+placeholders+approvalMap, add item to LIST_PROCESS, add item to LIST_ACTIVITY_LOG) into an async helper `createProcessForDocument(params)` with the ICreateProcessParams signature documented in plan.md. Resolve currentUser.Id once and pass it in.

Rewire handleSaveWorkflow (single flow) to call createProcessForDocument with `batch` undefined, passing current component state (approvers, placeholders, fileBlob, fileMetadata.fileRef, reviewerCanDownload, embedQrCode). Keep the LIST_PROCESS add payload byte-for-byte identical when batch is undefined (Title, HashHex, FileRef0, RequestorId, Status, ProcessData, UserNotif, isDownloadable).
When `params.batch` is provided, the helper's LIST_PROCESS add payload ALSO sets `BatchId: params.batch.batchId` and `BatchMode: params.batch.batchMode`.

Read `fileRefs` from the query string alongside the existing `fileRef`. If `fileRefs` is present and JSON-parses to an array of >=1 strings, enter batch mode; otherwise behave exactly as today (single-file path unchanged).

In batch mode, maintain per-document state so each document keeps its own approvers and placeholders (e.g. an array of document descriptors each holding fileRef, loaded blob, approvers[], placeholders[]). Load each PDF as the user navigates (or preload) using the existing fetch logic (getSP against the source site, getFileByServerRelativePath).

Add simple navigation between the N documents (stepper/tabs/list), reusing the existing PdfViewer and Sidebar for the currently selected document. Only extend Sidebar/IInitiateSignatureProps props if navigation/validation genuinely requires it; keep all existing single-flow props and behavior intact.

Validation before batch submit: every document must have >=1 approver, and every approver in a document must have >=1 placeholder box (same rule the single flow enforces). Block submit and clearly indicate which document is incomplete (reuse the existing validation dialog pattern or an equivalent).

On batch submit: generate one batchId via `crypto.randomUUID()` with a UUID v4 fallback; loop the documents calling `createProcessForDocument({ ..., batch: { batchId, batchMode: "AllOrNothing" } })` for each. If one document's creation throws mid-loop, surface a clear error and stop; do NOT delete already-created items. Add a code comment stating distributed rollback is out of scope.
Add a code comment noting the existing Power Automate flow triggers on item-created, so each created Process item fires its own initiate email automatically — no email code added here.
acceptance_criteria: A createProcessForDocument helper exists and is called by BOTH the single-flow save and the batch loop; the single-flow LIST_PROCESS payload is unchanged (no BatchId/BatchMode written for single requests).

With a `fileRefs` JSON-array query param, the page lets the user configure approvers+placeholders per document with navigation between documents, and blocks submit with a clear message when any document lacks an approver or a placeholder.
Batch submit creates one Approvals Process item per document, all sharing one BatchId and BatchMode='AllOrNothing', with all other per-item fields identical to the single flow.
When `fileRefs` is absent, the page behaves exactly as before (zero single-flow behavior change).
`npm run build` exits 0 with no TypeScript/ESLint errors.
verification: Run `npm run build` and confirm it exits 0 with no TypeScript or ESLint errors.
Code review: confirm the single-flow add payload is unchanged when batch is undefined and that BatchId/BatchMode are only written on the batch path.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED in src/webparts/initiateSignature/components/InitiateSignature.tsx. Build (npm run build) exits 0; only the 7 pre-existing lint warnings remain (ApprovalService.ts, EsignDataService.ts x3, UserService.ts, Sidebar.tsx x2) — none in InitiateSignature.tsx.

HELPER: extracted `createProcessForDocument(params: ICreateProcessParams)`. ICreateProcessParams = { fileRef: string; fileBlob: Blob; approvers: IApprover[]; placeholders: ISignaturePlaceholder[]; reviewerCanDownload: boolean; embedQrCode: boolean; currentUserId: number; spDoc: SPFI; spList: SPFI; batch?: { batchId: string; batchMode: string } }. It does QR-embed + setContentChunked overwrite, generatePDFHash, builds ProcessSignature JSON from approvers+placeholders+approvalMap, adds one LIST_PROCESS item and one LIST_ACTIVITY_LOG item. The LIST_PROCESS add payload is built as an object (Title, HashHex, FileRef0, RequestorId, Status, ProcessData, UserNotif, isDownloadable) and ONLY when params.batch is provided does it additionally set BatchId=batch.batchId and BatchMode=batch.batchMode. So the single-flow payload is byte-for-byte identical when batch is undefined (no BatchId/BatchMode written). currentUser.Id is resolved ONCE by the caller and passed in as currentUserId.

SINGLE FLOW: handleSaveWorkflow keeps its exact validation + Dialog behavior, resolves spDoc/spList/currentUser, then calls createProcessForDocument WITHOUT batch. Zero behavior change for single requests.

BATCH MODE DETECTION: reads `fileRefs` from the query string (alongside existing `fileRef`). Parsed in a useMemo `batchFileRefs` via JSON.parse; enters batch mode only if it is an array of >=1 strings (isBatchMode). When `fileRefs` is absent the single-file path is unchanged — the single-document fetch effect early-returns when isBatchMode is true and is otherwise identical (including the no-fileRef redirect).

PER-DOCUMENT STATE: interface IBatchDocument { fileRef; fileName; blob?: Blob; fileUrl?: string; approvers[]; placeholders[]; reviewerCanDownload; embedQrCode; loaded }. State: batchDocs: IBatchDocument[], activeDocIndex, batchValidationMessage, batchDialogVisible. A batch-load effect fetches every PDF once via getSP(context, sourcePage) + getFileByServerRelativePath(ref).getBlob() (same cross-site logic as single flow; sourcePage = `source` query param). Docs that fail to load get loaded=false. A mirror effect copies the active doc into the shared editing state (approvers/placeholders/fileBlob/fileUrl/fileMetadata/reviewerCanDownload/embedQrCode) so the EXISTING Sidebar + PdfViewer edit the active doc with NO prop changes. A write-back effect folds live edits back into batchDocs[activeDocIndex] so each doc keeps its own config across navigation.

NAVIGATION: a button bar above the PDF (rendered only in batch mode) lists all N docs; active=primary, complete=success(✓), incomplete=outline. Clicking sets activeDocIndex. No Sidebar/PdfViewer/IInitiateSignatureProps prop changes were needed.

VALIDATION + SUBMIT: Sidebar onSave is wired to handleBatchSubmit in batch mode (handleSaveWorkflow otherwise). handleBatchSubmit folds the live active-doc edits in, then validates every doc (must be loaded, >=1 approver, every approver has >=1 placeholder box); on failure it sets activeDocIndex to the offending doc and shows the 'Batch Incomplete' dialog. On success it generates one batchId via generateBatchId() (crypto.randomUUID with a getRandomValues UUID-v4 fallback), resolves currentUser once, and loops createProcessForDocument({...per-doc..., batch:{ batchId, batchMode:'AllOrNothing' }}). If one doc throws mid-loop it surfaces a clear message (naming how many were already created) and STOPS without deleting already-created items — a code comment states distributed rollback is out of scope. A 'Batch Success' dialog redirects back to the folder on OK.

EMAIL: a code comment notes the Power Automate flow triggers on item-created in LIST_PROCESS, so each created Process item fires its own initiate email automatically — no email code was added.

CONTRACT CONSUMED (from FEAT-001): fileRefs = JSON.parse of the decoded query param (URLSearchParams already decodes once) → string[] of server-relative FileRefs; `source` = the Finance library web absoluteUrl, passed as the base URL to getSP for cross-site reads. For FEAT-003 / approval-side work: each batch Process item carries BatchId (shared GUID) and BatchMode='AllOrNothing' SharePoint columns (created manually per context.json); all other per-item fields (Title, HashHex, FileRef0, RequestorId, Status='Processing', ProcessData, UserNotif, isDownloadable) are identical to the single flow.
